assignment: Explore this combination story through the normal player interface. Follow your curiosity; stop if satisfied, bored or confused. Completion is optional. Predict outcomes when you naturally have an expectation. Report concrete valued or confusing moments, pacing, continuity, and one useful next experiment. Do not try to please the designer. You may only use the supplied player CLI; do not inspect source, manuscript, saved session files, reports, developer routes or other players. This is logical play, not visual or touch evaluation.

playerEvidence.intention: Understand the immediate repair goal; radio is the straightforward survival route, but I noticed the alternate light-signal possibility.

playerEvidence.expected: The cable repairs the radio but probably still needs battery power.
playerEvidence.alternatives: I could build the light signal instead, but repair seems less elaborate.

playerEvidence.intention: Charge the battery so the repaired radio can transmit.
Place the working radio on the ridge to contact the orbiter.
playerEvidence.experience: The charger surviving radio assembly is encouraging: the light branch remains available rather than spent.

playerEvidence.expected: An answer from the orbiter should explain what survival step matters next.

playerEvidence.experience: The orbiter answer makes the short first sequence feel purposeful. The next paragraph is much denser, but three visible goals let me pick water first.

playerEvidence.intention: Use the explicitly described portable heater connection to melt water.
playerEvidence.alternatives: The solar charger also works here, but using a heater for ice feels more direct.

playerEvidence.expected: Relocating the already built radio should mark the refuge. I do not need to rebuild a beacon.
playerEvidence.experience: Dirty water leaves an obvious future need, but there is no filter yet, so I will handle the remaining goals.

playerEvidence.expected: Seal or flatten the patch before fitting it to the hatch. The partner list teaches this ordering; I might otherwise have tried the frame first.

playerEvidence.experience: The patch surviving as a separate item after becoming a sealed panel is a little odd; I read that as spare patch material rather than the same object.

playerEvidence.intention: Insulate before securing; I want to see whether either order is acceptable.

playerEvidence.experience: The five-stage vestibule build was intelligible but mostly a chain of prompted material upgrades. Choosing insulation before tie downs gave a small sense of control, not a different plan.
Filtering pays off the dirty-water detail I noticed outside. Planting seeds is a larger time commitment than waiting for rescue; I am curious whether the story acknowledges that shift.

playerEvidence.intention: Plant before watering because that is the natural sequence to me.
playerEvidence.alternatives: Water can apparently go straight on seeds, but I do not know where those wet seeds would be held.

playerEvidence.intention: Cover it before leaving it warm so the growing tray is protected all along.

playerEvidence.expected: A time passage should germinate the seeds, now watered and protected.

playerEvidence.experience: The warm-habitat combination jumped straight to Propagator. The chapter said this takes time, but no moment marked that elapsed time; I am less clear whether I have seedlings or just equipment.

I understand the rover objectives but not why I should leave the marked refuge for the outcrop. I will explore the viewing equipment because finding a route is more interesting than another build chain.

playerEvidence.expected: A telescope to survey the route visually, perhaps an alternative to photographs.
A zoomed camera view for distant route landmarks.
playerEvidence.experience: The telescope cannot be read or used directly at the overlook in the presented actions. My visual-survey idea has become the photograph route after all.

playerEvidence.intention: Set the telescope camera at the overlook to survey the landmarks.
playerEvidence.expected: A photograph or a new camera action should become available at the viewpoint.

playerEvidence.intention: Try actively using rather than merely placing the camera at the overlook.
playerEvidence.experience: Placing it did nothing. I cannot tell if the telescope is decorative, for a later chapter, or not the supported camera the prose means.

playerEvidence.intention: Fall back to the plain supported camera the paragraph probably meant.
playerEvidence.experience: The telescope path felt like a reasonable inference that led nowhere useful here. The remaining separate Camera and Tripod let me recover, but also make the assembled telescope camera feel oddly nonphysical.

The plain field camera works where the telescope camera did not, without explanation. Also the photograph is not readable, so finding a route is another object merge rather than interpreting landmarks myself.

intelligibility.explanation: Immediate repair, power, water and planting goals were clear. The telescope camera looked appropriate for the route overlook but neither placement nor active use helped; a plain field camera did, with no explanation of the distinction.

learning.explanation: Item names and visible partner actions taught local ordering, and I could predict several results. Most learning was recognizing the next permitted pair, not applying a general rule: the supported telescope camera did not transfer to a viewpoint where the supported field camera worked.

construction.explanation: Repairing then powering a radio and building a secure insulated vestibule made coherent artifacts. Later construction became chains of renamed objects. Combining telescope and camera did not visibly deliver the use I built it for, and the route photograph could not be inspected, only merged.

pacing.explanation: The brief radio sequence reached an orbiter answer promptly. The five-stage vestibule and five-stage growing task then felt increasingly procedural. Germination had no visible elapsed-time beat. I stopped before another rover build after my navigation curiosity became another merge rather than a discovery.

continuity.explanation: Reusing the radio at the refuge and later filtering water collected outside gave the world useful continuity. But patch and camera components surviving assembly were physically unclear, time passage for seedlings was thin, and the move from marking a refuge to leaving for an outcrop lacked a stated motive.

choice.explanation: I chose radio over the visible light route, heater over solar melting, insulation before tie downs, and planting before watering. These were understandable local options. The exploratory telescope choice led to an unexplained dead end at the relevant viewpoint, while successful navigation required the plain camera chain.

playerReport.experience: Logical-only fresh AI player evidence, not a human enjoyment or touch/UI test. Valued moments: the orbiter answer after placing my powered radio, moving that same radio to mark the refuge, and returning to the previously collected dirty water with a filter. My main confusion was building a supported telescope camera for surveying, then finding that it could not do what the plain supported camera could. Combining remained intelligible as material assembly but was becoming less meaningful as choice or observation; the route image was just another ingredient rather than something I could learn from.
playerReport.stoppingReason: Voluntarily stopped after event 31 in chapter index 3, incomplete, with rover power and harness goals remaining. Not budget exhaustion. I had recovered from the telescope detour and solved the route, but curiosity had diminished and I did not want another prompted construction chain without understanding why we were leaving the refuge.
playerReport.nextExperiment: Give a fresh player the route chapter with a clear reason to travel and a short visible observation when each viewing device is used. Test whether Telescope camera can satisfy the supported-photograph task, or explain concretely why it cannot. Ask the player what they learned about the route before revealing the next pair; distinguish understanding and renewed curiosity from mere completion.
